title: Is it possible to make a sandbox type game with MV, similar to Animal Crossing/Furcadia?

posts.author: Aevisia
posts.body: I have an idea where I want users to be able to build up their own towns and farms, similar to Animal Crossing where it's structured and there's a set amount of things that can be built and the players can choose the placement/layout of said structures, but similar to Furcadia in the sense that users could potentially import their own assets/tilesheets/sprites/etc to really make their town/farm their own if they want to. Would this be possible to create in RPG Maker MV?

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
The code for the game is in the js folder for you to access and modify - it is possible to do whatever you want.
That said, the further you depart from the traditional JRPG that the software is designed to recreate, the harder it's going to be.
Your basic premise of building things is already pretty challenging and requires some complex setups using plugins to change tiles on a map. The notion of giving your players an interface to somehow import their own assets...you're looking at a lot of custom code.
You'd either need to spend a lot of time becoming proficient with JavaScript or spend some significant money hiring someone to make that for you.
I think other engines (Unreal/Unity?) have more built-in mod support that would make you start much closer to your goal.

I stopped working on that project, but it's not that hard to do really.
You will need to learn javascript, NodeJS and database handling (we used MySQL, but the newer MariaDB or MongoDB would be better)
On the plugin end you put emitters to send data to the NodeJS server
On the NodeJS server you put emitters to send data to the plugin
using NodeJS's
Emitter.on
and
Emitter.emit
features
And on the server side you establish a connection with the database and communicate with it based on emitters data received or requests.
However, my project (along with geonidas) was not very stable or powerful enough for active co-op.
My guess is, you would be better off using KageDesu -
Discord
as they have tons off plugins that are helpful for different situations.
I am working on a LUA server concept along with LUA integration (to allow people to code their plugins in LUA and their serverside in LUA), but this is just a premice and nowhere near available.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
About Co-OP:
you will have two big and difficult main problems trying to implement that:
First, all RMs are pure single player, they have no way of handling multiple inputs and multiple active players in the engine. To change that will not be easy.
You might want to check himeworks.com however, iirc then Tsukihime had made a party manager that allows for one active and multiple inactive parties, that would be a first step toward multiple active players/parties.
Second, no RM contains any network code for implementing anything. Which means you'll need to implement that code from scratch, and that again needs a lot of knowledge - knowledge that goes beyond javascript depending on what you want.
MMO and any high number of coop will require a server for coordinating, and it is rather unlikely that simple javascript can handle that - you'll have to learn at minimum SQL and probably a server programming language in addition to javascript.
With a low number of coop players ( 2 or max 4 or so) you might be able to pull this off without a server and using a local network instead of the internet - that would be easier but still not easy.

ANETZ by PKD will
kind of
achieve this for you.
Servers aren't created by the player Host though, the plugin author has set up a global server the game session will be hosted on. He also created a server for the plugin that creators can use to run their own servers but that is run on the Game creators hardware or virtual server you already own. Not via the host player's hardware/server.
It has some other limitations to it, like no server side maps so events only update in real time for player's on the same map(the biggest, on the face, limitation I have found). But it is easy enough to use and he has a decent collection of plugins that are compatible, including one that allows you to place events on the map(ie. furniture) and an ABS. In the last two months he has also added MZ(MV)3D support as well.
Ignore all the "Z's", all of his plugins are supported on both MV and MZ. So ANETZ will work on MV.
I have yet to find a plugin though that will allow player's on a server to change tiles though. So stuff like making roads will be hard to pull off if that's something you were planning. I've tried three to date and I haven't been able to get this to work(for obvious reasons).
